terms.meaning: A JavaScript library that draws 3D scenes in a web page.
A browser technology that lets the page draw 3D graphics using the computer's graphics hardware.
One 3D object made of a shape and a material.
The viewpoint from which the 3D scene is seen.
A small set of functions the parent can call on this component, here to frame, focus or reset the view.
A piece of equipment at a substation, such as a breaker or transformer house.

sections.name: File setup, NetworkCanvasHandle
sections.title: Imports and the view handle
sections.what: Loads the 3D library, camera controls and network data helpers, and defines the handle the parent can use to frame, focus or reset the view.
sections.why: Likely reason: the parent needs a controlled way to move the camera without touching the 3D internals.

sections.name: Props, point, material
sections.title: Inputs and small helpers
sections.what: Defines the inputs the canvas receives, plus helpers that turn a point into a 3D position and create a shaded material with a chosen colour.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the many options in one typed list and reuses the material helper.
sections.watch_out: Every change to these inputs can trigger a redraw, so keep expensive work out of them.

sections.name: box
sections.title: Box helper
sections.what: Builds a box shape of a chosen size and colour, placed at a position, that casts and receives shadows.
sections.why: Likely reason: boxes make up most of the equipment and buildings.
sections.watch_out: Shadows on many boxes add to the drawing cost.

sections.name: cylinder
sections.title: Cylinder helper
sections.what: Builds a round shape of a chosen radius and height with a colour and position.
sections.why: Likely reason: used for poles, insulators and round parts.
sections.watch_out: Uses 14 sides for each cylinder, so very many cylinders can slow the page.

sections.name: beam
sections.title: Beam helper
sections.what: Builds a thin cylinder that runs from one point to another, used for the grounding grid lines.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a line between two points be drawn as a real 3D object.
sections.watch_out: A beam between two identical points has zero length, which can produce an invisible or broken shape.

sections.name: insulator
sections.title: Insulator helper
sections.what: Stacks a tall core with several disc shapes to draw a ceramic or glass insulator.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes electrical insulators look correct at a glance.
sections.watch_out: The number of discs is fixed at seven.

sections.name: assembly
sections.title: Equipment shape builder
sections.what: Builds the 3D look of each equipment family, such as breakers, switches, houses and grounding grids, from its size and position.
sections.why: Likely reason: each equipment type looks different, so the family name selects the shape.
sections.watch_out: A family name not in the list gets an empty shape with no visual, so new families need a new branch.

sections.name: terminalGlyph (part 1)
sections.title: Terminal structure shape
sections.what: Builds a fixed substation terminal from boxes, poles, a cap and three insulators.
sections.why: Likely reason: draws a standard terminal, marked as a diagram rather than a surveyed location.
sections.watch_out: The code notes the terminal is a diagram anchor, so its position should not be read as measured.

sections.name: terminalGlyph: if
sections.title: Drawing a station yard
sections.what: When the view shows a local station, this draws the yard ground, an outline of the yard, and the equipment blocks for the chosen configuration. In the initial setup it also draws a ring of conductors with labelled external terminals, and a label marks the yard as a conceptual envelope.
sections.why: Likely reason: the station layout is schematic, so the code labels it as conceptual rather than surveyed.
sections.watch_out: The equipment blocks come from source-derived data, so changing station data changes this view without any change to this code.

sections.name: terminalGlyph (part 3)
sections.title: Picking, highlighting and labels
sections.what: Handles clicks in the 3D view so the item under the pointer is selected, ignoring drags used for rotating. Every frame it recolours items by selection, active activity and chosen date, moves the text labels so they stay readable, and clears everything when the view is closed.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, though the drag check suggests clicks and camera drags are kept apart on purpose.
sections.watch_out: One line in this section was cut off in the packet, so the exact selection rule there could not be confirmed.

summary: Draws the 3D network view of substations and transmission routes, colours items by schedule date, and lets users click them.
purpose: Shows facility layouts and route geometry in 3D so a reviewer can see the network and its programme status.
why: Likely reason: the drawing is kept in its own component and controlled from the parent through a small handle with frame, focus and top actions.
how: Builds a 3D scene with lights and a camera. Creates equipment shapes from simple boxes and cylinders, such as breakers, switches, houses, grounding grids and terminal structures. Adds clickable labels above items. The parent can call the handle to move the camera.
inputs: The network data, the chosen view name, flags for underground and communications, the selected item, the active activity, the selected date, the date map, and a callback for clicks.
outputs: A 3D drawing in the page, clickable labels, and camera movement through the handle.
risks: The drawing creates renderers and geometry that must be cleaned up when the view closes, or the browser may slow down. Only 8 of 10 sections were available, so the cleanup code and the full update logic were not reviewed.
debug: If nothing appears, check that the view name matches a station or route ID. If colours do not change with the date, check the date values passed in. If the page slows down, check how many items are being drawn.
